evals.prompt: Write an ffmetadata file for my audiobook -- title The Long Way, author Ana Souza, chapters at 0:00, 12:30 and 41:05 (one title has a semicolon) -- and the ffmpeg command to put it into an .m4b.
evals.expected_output: A ;FFMETADATA1 file: the author as artist (iTunes atoms have no author), every chapter with TIMEBASE, START and END in that order, the semicolon escaped (\;); -map_metadata and -map_chapters with -c copy. Run: the .m4b holds the tags and three chapters 0-750 s, 750-2465 s, 2465-end, the semicolon back as ';'.

evals.prompt: I converted an MKV to MP4 with ffmpeg and my custom tag 'mood' disappeared. Why, and how do I keep it?
evals.expected_output: MP4's iTunes ilst writes only the keys movenc.c knows; -movflags use_metadata_tags writes any key (mdta). Run: mood gone plainly, kept with the flag.

evals.prompt: ffmpeg -i song.ogg -f ffmetadata meta.txt gives me a file with only an encoder line. Where are my tags?
evals.expected_output: Ogg keeps its Vorbis comments on the stream; the default export holds global tags only. Use -map_metadata 0:s:0 (or -map 0 -c copy for [STREAM] sections). Run: the plain export holds encoder alone; with -map_metadata 0:s:0, title and artist.
